race_context: The 'Clinton Central School Board' seats belong to Clinton Central School Corporation, based in Michigantown in Clinton County, which runs two schools: Clinton Central Elementary and Clinton Central Jr./Sr. High School {cc_home}{nces_cc}. Federal data list 902 students in 2024-25 {nces_cc}. Levi Yowell is superintendent {cc_staff}{cc_min_0720}.

The board has seven members: six seats carry area labels (Warren, Sugar Creek, Kirklin, Michigantown, Forest and Johnson) and one is at large {cc_board}. Current members are Joshua Davison (president), Amy Mennen (vice president), Gina Crenshaw (secretary), Katie Cohee, Bryce Eaton, Travis Robinson and Kyle Rule {cc_board}{cc_min_0720}. This guide did not find the district's written election plan, so it could not confirm whether every voter in the corporation votes for every seat.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: three seats, each electing one member, consistent with the state list's 'vote for 1' {in_list}{ft_2022_results}. In 2022, Gina Crenshaw won District 10 over Craig Sheets (65.98% to 34.02%), Katie Cohee won District 12 unopposed and Bryce Eaton won the At Large seat unopposed {ft_2022_results}. The board's member page labels Crenshaw's seat Kirklin, Cohee's Sugar Creek and Eaton's At Large {cc_board}.

Who is running: none of the three members elected in 2022 (Crenshaw, Cohee, Eaton) is on the 2026 ballot, so all three seats will have new members {in_list}{ft_2022_results}. Jessica Jacobs (Nonpartisan) is unopposed in District 10, Melanie Harden (Republican) is unopposed in District 12, and Brett Hillis and Mark A McClain, both Republicans, are running for the At Large seat {in_list}.

Party labels and filing: a 2025 state law (Senate Enrolled Act 287) let school board candidates list a party for the first time in 2026 {ft_party_split}. Clinton County Daily News reported, citing Clinton County Red for Public Ed, that 11 school board seats across the county would be on the fall ballot {ccdn_filing_2026}.

Facilities and debt (2026): the board held a first preliminary determination hearing on a 2026 general obligation (G.O.) bond on June 15, 2026 {cc_min_0615}. On July 20, 2026 it voted 7-0 to adopt the bond's project resolution, preliminary determination resolution, preliminary bond resolution and reimbursement resolution {cc_min_0720}. The Sept. 21, 2026 agenda listed a hearing on an additional appropriation for the bond and a final bond resolution {cc_agenda_0921}. This guide did not find the bond's amount or the projects it would fund.

Budget and property taxes: Clinton Central voters approved an operating referendum in May 2023, a tax rate of $0.15 per $100 of assessed value for eight years, estimated to raise about $675,000 a year {wfyi_ref_2023}. The board held a 2027 budget workshop on Aug. 31, 2026 and a 2027 budget hearing was on the Sept. 21 agenda {cc_min_0831}{cc_agenda_0921}. On June 29, 2026 the board approved a resolution for 2026 transfers between the debt service and operations funds {cc_min_0629}. This guide found no reporting on how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects the district.

Partnerships and programs: on July 20, 2026 the board approved a Clinton Carroll joint services agreement and a memorandum of understanding with the Boys & Girls Club {cc_min_0720}. At the June 15 meeting a board member asked about before- and after-school care, and the minutes note the Boys & Girls Club was still interested and working on staffing {cc_min_0615}.

Policies: the July 20, 2026 agenda included policies on wireless devices, student discipline, board vacancies, social media use by board members, restraint and seclusion, and police relations {cc_agenda_0720}. On Aug. 31, 2026 the board adopted a student attendance and truancy prevention policy (Policy 4320) and voted to retire older policies, and approved, pending attorney review, a naming-rights agreement for a new athletic entrance tied to a donation {cc_min_0831}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of the candidates' views. Board meetings are held at 6 p.m. at the district office and broadcast on the district's YouTube channel; the next is Oct. 19, 2026 {cc_portal}{cc_board_welcome}.
